Chapter 12: The Joy of Being.
Underneath all the striving and searching, there’s a simple kind of joy that comes from just being alive. It’s not tied to your circumstances, your achievements, or anything you own. Instead, it’s that quiet happiness that starts to show up when your mind finally settles, your heart opens up, and you’re fully present in the moment.
Picture yourself sitting in a park. You feel the sun warming your face, there’s a gentle breeze on your skin, and you hear the laughter of children somewhere close by. There’s nothing you have to do, nothing you need to achieve, and nothing that needs fixing. In that space, a gentle joy rises up—a feeling of being completely at home in the world.
Now, this kind of joy isn’t like excitement, or the rush you get from pleasure. It’s quieter, deeper, and it tends to last much longer. It’s our natural state—the one that shows up when we let go of constant thoughts, worries, and the urge to keep striving. Most of us catch glimpses of this joy in moments of beauty, connection, or when everything is still. But the beautiful thing is, it’s always there, just waiting for us to remember it.
If you’re someone who’s struggling with depression, the idea of joy might feel a million miles away—or maybe even impossible. But even in the toughest moments, there are these tiny openings—a kind word, a moment of rest, or just a single breath of fresh air. By gently bringing your attention to those moments, no matter how brief, you start to let the light of joy back in.
The joy of being isn’t something you have to earn or achieve—it’s your birthright. It’s the very essence of life itself. And you won’t find it in the future; it’s right here, in the heart of this present moment.
Think about a child, lost in play. They’re totally engaged, completely alive, and not worrying about the past or the future. As adults, we can come back to that state—not by becoming childish, but by letting go of the weight of our thoughts and remembering the simple joy of just being.
Most of us spend our lives looking for happiness outside ourselves. But the greatest joy is always found within, in that quiet presence that’s never left us. In this space, life doesn’t have to be a problem to solve. It can simply be a mystery to live.
